newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas edges higher on colder weather.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas edges higher on colder weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were driven higher again Thursday by a late-winter chill across Canada and the midwestern and northeast U.S., market sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices gained another three cents to C$1.48-1.49 per gigajoule (GJ) amid below-freezing temperatures in Alberta.
"This cold snap is very short-lived. Utilities are out there buying today, but that should taper off," one Calgary-based source said.
In Calgary, temperatures were hovering around -15 degrees Celsius today, traders said.

However, warmer forecasts for this weekend and early next week kept the lid on other AECO prices. The thermometer is forecast to climb to about zero on Saturday and then to about +4 degrees C on Sunday.
April AECO prices slipped about four to five cents to just under C$1.40 per GJ, while summer business was done around C$1.41, traders said.

At Sumas, Wash., prices rose by about two cents to $1.18-1.23 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) as hot temperatures blanketed the West Coast and were forecast to continue through early next week.
At Niagara, prices firmed by four cents to the low-to-mid $2.20s per mmBtu amid cold, snowy weather.
